sentences.en: When you bite into a sweet apple, you probably do not think about bees.
sentences.zh: 当你咬下一口甜甜的苹果时，你大概不会想到蜜蜂。

sentences.en: But without bees and other pollinators, that apple could not exist at all.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有蜜蜂和其他传粉者，那只苹果根本不会存在。

sentences.en: Scientists say that about one third of the food we eat depends on animal pollinators.
sentences.zh: 科学家说，我们吃的食物大约有三分之一依赖动物传粉。

sentences.en: Apples, watermelons, cherries, tomatoes, and almonds all need help from small creatures.
sentences.zh: 苹果、西瓜、樱桃、番茄和杏仁，都离不开小动物们的帮忙。

sentences.en: To understand why, you need a little basic biology.
sentences.zh: 要弄清原因，你需要一点基础的生物学知识。

sentences.en: A flower is not only beautiful; it is a machine for making seeds.
sentences.zh: 花不仅美丽，它还是一台制造种子的机器。

sentences.en: To make seeds, pollen must travel from one flower to another.
sentences.zh: 要结出种子，花粉必须从一朵花传到另一朵花。

sentences.en: This process is called pollination.
sentences.zh: 这个过程叫做授粉。

sentences.en: Some plants, like corn and wheat, use the wind to transfer their pollen.
sentences.zh: 有些植物，比如玉米和小麦，靠风来传送花粉。

sentences.en: For them, the wind is a free transport service.
sentences.zh: 对它们来说，风就是免费的运输服务。

sentences.en: But many fruit trees and vegetables depend on insects instead.
sentences.zh: 但许多果树和蔬菜依靠的却是昆虫。

sentences.en: This is where the bee comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就轮到蜜蜂登场了。

sentences.en: A bee does not intend to help the flowers; it is only looking for food.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂并不是有意帮助花朵，它只是在寻找食物。

sentences.en: It lands on a flower and drinks the sweet liquid called nectar.
sentences.zh: 它落在花上，吸食那种叫花蜜的甜液。

sentences.en: It also collects pollen, a yellow powder full of protein, to feed its young at home.
sentences.zh: 它还采集花粉——一种富含蛋白质的黄色粉末——带回家喂幼虫。

sentences.en: A bee's body is covered with tiny, branched hairs.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂的身体覆盖着细小的分支绒毛。

sentences.en: As it moves inside the flower, pollen sticks to the hairs like dust to a sweater.
sentences.zh: 它在花里爬动时，花粉便粘在绒毛上，就像灰尘粘在毛衣上。

sentences.en: When the bee flies to the next flower, some of the pollen rubs off.
sentences.zh: 当蜜蜂飞到下一朵花时，一部分花粉就被蹭了下来。

sentences.en: If that pollen lands on exactly the right part of the new flower, seeds begin to form.
sentences.zh: 如果这些花粉恰好落在新花的正确部位，种子就开始形成。

sentences.en: In this way, a bee transfers pollen from flower to flower all day long.
sentences.zh: 就这样，蜜蜂整日把花粉从一朵花搬到另一朵花。

sentences.en: A single honeybee may visit hundreds of flowers in one day.
sentences.zh: 一只蜜蜂一天可以造访数百朵花。

sentences.en: And a healthy colony may contain more than fifty thousand workers.
sentences.zh: 而一个健康的蜂群可以拥有五万多名"工人"。

sentences.en: Numbers like these make bees the most important pollinators on earth.
sentences.zh: 这样的数量使蜜蜂成为地球上最重要的传粉者。

sentences.en: Bees do even more than carry pollen.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂做的还不止搬运花粉。

sentences.en: Inside the hive, they share information in an amazing way.
sentences.zh: 在蜂巢里，它们以一种惊人的方式共享信息。

sentences.en: When a bee finds a rich field of flowers, it returns home and performs a dance.
sentences.zh: 当一只蜜蜂找到一片花田，它会飞回巢里跳一支舞。

sentences.en: The direction and the length of the dance report the location and distance of the food.
sentences.zh: 舞蹈的方向和时长，报告的就是食物的位置和距离。

sentences.en: Other bees watch the dance and then fly straight to the flowers.
sentences.zh: 其他蜜蜂看完舞蹈，便直奔花田而去。

sentences.en: It is as if the hive had its own tiny newspaper.
sentences.zh: 这就好比蜂群拥有自己的一份微型报纸。

sentences.en: Karl von Frisch, the scientist who first described this dance, won a Nobel Prize for the discovery in 1973.
sentences.zh: 最早描述这种舞蹈的科学家卡尔·冯·弗里施，因此项发现于1973年获得诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: Sadly, the world of bees is facing serious problems.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，蜜蜂的世界正面临严峻的问题。

sentences.en: In many countries, beekeepers have reported the sudden loss of whole colonies.
sentences.zh: 在许多国家，养蜂人报告过整群蜜蜂突然消失的怪事。

sentences.en: Scientists believe there is no single cause.
sentences.zh: 科学家们认为原因并不单一。

sentences.en: New diseases, some farm chemicals, and the loss of wild flowers often occur together.
sentences.zh: 新病害、某些农用化学品和野花的消失常常同时出现。

sentences.en: When one problem appears, the others quickly make it worse.
sentences.zh: 一个问题出现时，其他问题会迅速令其恶化。

sentences.en: If bees disappeared, our dinner table would change completely.
sentences.zh: 如果蜜蜂消失，我们的餐桌将彻底改变。

sentences.en: A world without bees would still have corn and rice, which are wind-pollinated.
sentences.zh: 没有蜜蜂的世界仍会有靠风传粉的玉米和水稻。

sentences.en: But apples and cherries would become rare and expensive.
sentences.zh: 但苹果和樱桃将变得稀有而昂贵。

sentences.en: Fortunately, everyone can do something to help.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，每个人都能帮上忙。

sentences.en: Planting flowers on a balcony or in a school garden gives city bees the food they need.
sentences.zh: 在阳台或校园花园里种花，就能给城里的蜜蜂提供所需的食物。

sentences.en: Choosing not to spray chemicals while flowers are blooming also protects them.
sentences.zh: 在开花期不喷洒化学药剂，同样能保护它们。

sentences.en: Even leaving a small corner of the garden wild can provide a home for wild bees.
sentences.zh: 哪怕留一小块园地任其荒长，也能给野生蜜蜂提供家园。

sentences.en: Bees work quietly and never ask for thanks.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂默默工作，从不求人感谢。

sentences.en: But our fruit, our seeds, and the whole natural system depend on them.
sentences.zh: 但我们的水果、种子乃至整个自然系统都依赖于它们。

sentences.en: The next time you eat a sweet apple, remember the small, fuzzy worker that made it possible.
sentences.zh: 下次吃甜苹果时，请记得那个让它成为可能的小小毛茸茸工人。

questions.q: About how much of the food we eat depends on animal pollinators?
questions.explain: "about one third of the food we eat depends on animal pollinators" —— 约三分之一。

questions.q: Why does pollen stick to a bee's body?
options: Its body is covered with tiny branched hairs.
Bees carry it in their mouths.
Flowers glue it on with nectar.
questions.explain: "A bee's body is covered with tiny, branched hairs"，花粉像灰尘粘毛衣一样粘上去。

questions.q: What does a bee's dance inside the hive do?
options: It asks the queen for food.
It reports the location and distance of flowers.
It warns the colony of rain.
It celebrates the end of the day.
questions.explain: 舞蹈的方向和时长 "report the location and distance of the food"。

questions.q: Which of these would probably become rare if bees disappeared?
questions.explain: 玉米水稻靠风传粉仍会存在，而苹果樱桃等依赖昆虫，会变得"rare and expensive"。

questions.q: According to the passage, what can people do to help bees?
options: Plant flowers and avoid spraying chemicals when flowers bloom.
Cut down trees around the city.
questions.explain: 结尾的三条建议：种花、开花期不喷药、留小块野地。
